CHROMIUM: alt-syscall: Add ARM64 support Update the whitelists so that they build for ARM64. The two major changes required for ARM64 support are: - Remove deprecated syscalls (e.g. open(), pipe()) which are not wired up on ARM64. - Account for the differences between ARM and IA32 in the compat tables. BUG=b:26733456 TEST=Builds for oak. Change-Id: I83c764db3fd03ac22c2cfe29bf81e26c4df44223 Signed-off-by: Andrew Bresticker <abrestic@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/323404 Tested-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dylan Reid <dgreid@chromium.org> (cherry picked from commit 6bf296053e9aeee54e2433174a03b7d2826ccf41) Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/324111

verify_components: add without goofy mode, fix UI display In CL:320884, the UI is accidentally disabled (the UI thread is not started at all). UI.Run() is called now. Add argument 'with_goofy' (default True), when this is set to False, user interface and event log is disabled. This will be used in run in test, where Goofy is not available. Without Goofy, we will not have user interface and might not have CROS_FACTORY_TEST_PATH (used by event log). Modify HWSEQ read logic to call ignore_error. In the current HWSEQ read function implementation of flashrom When a region is locked or has write-only permissions, read returns error immediately and the later regions are ignored. As it is, read happens in 64 byte chunks. If SPI_ACCESS_DENIED error is returned for a chunk, check if it can be ignored. If yes, fill the current chunk with 0xff and continue with the next block instead of returning error. BUG=chrome-os-partner:49474 TEST=flashrom -p host -r image.bin When ME is locked, image.bin will contain data of all regions except ME which will be all 0xFFs. Change-Id: Ic1eb59d5653820c2535cf7c335d6ea54d21c058a Signed-off-by: Ramya Vijaykumar <ramya.vijaykumar@intel.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/322078 Reviewed-by: David Hendricks <dhendrix@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Duncan Laurie <dlaurie@chromium.org>
